chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

"Only a believer is commanded to enjoin what is right and forbidden to prohibit what is wrong, so he admonishes; or an ignorant person, so he learns. As for the owner of the whip and sword, [he does not]."

key_terms.صَاحِبُ سَوْطٍ وَسَيْفٍ: the owner of the whip and sword (ruler/authority)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a believer's and a ruler's method of enjoining good according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the proper conduct of enjoining good by distinguishing between the believer’s gentle admonition or educational approach for the ignorant, and the ruler’s use of coercive force. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tarbiyah* (education) over *tarhib* (punishment) for the general populace, reserving the 'whip and sword' for authoritative enforcement. It highlights that moral correction is primarily a pedagogical duty for the faithful, while physical compulsion is the domain of governance.
